- **Compression** is the process of **reducing the dynamic range** of a signal using a **transfer function**. Compressors are usually used to **dynamically manage the volume** of a specific sound source, in order to **improve consistency during mixing and mastering**.

<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->
## Faust: Compression {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 85%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- **Compression** is the process of **reducing the dynamic range** of a signal using a **transfer function**. Compressors are usually used to **dynamically manage the volume** of a specific sound source, in order to **improve consistency during mixing and mastering**.
:::
- **Control parameters** are usually the following:
  - **Threshold** (*dB*): the level above which the amplitude of a signal is going to be reduced.
  - **Ratio**: the reduction factor when amplitude is above the threshold. 
  - **Attack** (*ms*): the speed at which compression is applied.
  - **Release** (*ms*): the speed at which compression is released.
  - **Makeup gain** (*dB*): final gain applied to the compressed signal.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
::: {.content style="padding-left: 5%; width: 110%;"}
{{< compressor >}}
:::
:::
::::

<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->
## Faust: Compression {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 85%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
:::
- A **Limiter** is a compressor with a (very) *high ratio* (usually *10:1* or more) and a *fast attack-time*.
It is generally used to ensure an ***audio signal never exceeds the amplitude of the threshold***,
to either *prevent distortion or damage* to PA speakers in a live situation, or to *make a
sound appear louder* in a **mixing/mastering context**. 
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
::: {.content style="padding-left: 5%; width: 110%;"}
{{< compressor mode=static >}}
:::
:::
::::
